body.statement:
Let \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), put \(A=A(\eta)\), \(F_k=\operatorname{de}_{G_0(\eta)}(T_k(\eta))\cap V\), and let \(H\) be the observational skeleton.  In the causally sufficient childless-selection pre-treatment twin construction, Dai et al.'s Lemmas 3--6 give the following facts.  Observational adjacency is generated by a basal observed edge or by an observed common child that is ancestral to selection.  An observed pair is adjacent in regime \(k\) exactly when it is observationally adjacent or its endpoints are joined in \(H[A]\) by a path whose internal vertices belong to \(F_k\cap A\).  The indicator-neighbor set is
\[
\operatorname{adj}_{M_k(\eta)}(\zeta_k)\cap V
=T_k(\eta)\cup\bigl((F_k\setminus T_k(\eta))\cap A\bigr).
\]
Every indicator edge is oriented out of \(\zeta_k\).  An observed directed edge of the observational MAG is retained in the regime MAG.  For any other regime adjacency \(xy\), its marks are determined as follows: two unaffected endpoints give \(x\mathbin{-}y\); if \(y\) is affected and either \(x\) is unaffected or \(x\in\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta)}(y)\), the edge is \(x\to y\); the symmetric condition gives \(y\to x\); and two affected endpoints with neither ancestral to the other give \(x\leftrightarrow y\).  In particular, observational endpoints inside \(A\) are tails, and an observational adjacency meeting \(V\setminus A\) is a basal directed edge with its basal orientation.

source.locator: Lemmas 3--6, main text pp. 6--7 and proofs in Appendix B

body.gap: The cited result does not contain the replacement construction or any cross-regime faithful-kernel realization.
body.consumer: It is used by the graphical replacement, retained-edge, and observable selectedness proofs.
